subject: Renewal: alignment on sprint credits, commit cadence & temporary rate guard
messages:
From: Sasha Petrova <sasha@auroraedge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auroraedge.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal request + sprint credits / temporary price guard

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Hope you’re both well. We’re coming up on our 12/31 renewal for AuroraEdge and wanted to get ahead of terms. A few items on our side:

- We expect a ~20% increase in peak inference over the next 6 months due to a new feature launch. Given that, we’re asking for a) a one-time sprint credit to help cover onboarding traffic (~50k token-equivalents), b) a 3-month temporary rate guard (price hold) while we ramp, and c) an adjusted commit cadence that moves us from monthly true-ups to a quarterly true-up to better match our billing cycles.

Attached is a short summary of expected usage and our legal/procurement asks (AuroraEdge_Renewal_Request.pdf). Our procurement team asked if Redwood can present a counter with 1) committed token bands, 2) a sprint credit bucket, and 3) a mechanism for a short-term price hold while our new feature stabilizes. If we can get something on paper this week, we can route PO and sign-off early next week.

Would you be able to share options and an internal lead to work out the precise pricing?

Thanks — Sasha
Sasha Petrova
Head of Platform, AuroraEdge
(attachment: AuroraEdge_Renewal_Request.pdf (pdf))

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Petrova <sasha@auroraedge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + sprint credits / temporary price guard

Thanks Sasha — appreciate the detail and the attachment.

Quick read: we can support a sprint credit, temporary rate guard, and move to quarterly true-ups; we’ll need to align internally on the size of the sprint credit and the discount bands tied to the new commit.

I’ve sketched three options below (high-level) — I’ll follow up with an internal note asking finance for a quick sign-off on one of these:

Option A — Conservative
- Commit: +10% from current baseline (month-over-month)
- Sprint credit: 25k tokens one-time
- Rate guard: 6 weeks post-launch at current price; afterwards revert to baseline pricing
- Discount: 12% on the bumped commit band

Option B — Balanced (recommended for AuroraEdge given ramp plan)
- Commit: +20% baseline (quarterly true-up)
- Sprint credit: 50k tokens one-time
- Rate guard: 3 months price hold for the bumped band
- Discount: 18% on bumped band; temporary extra 3% if PO is in by 12/08

Option C — Aggressive Upsell
- Commit: +35% baseline with stepped true-ups
- Sprint credit: 75k tokens + 20k onboarding buffer
- Rate guard: 3 months + option to extend to 6 months with usage gates
- Discount: 22% on bumped band with volume milestone credits

Couple of asks for you, Sasha: 1) Which option aligns with AuroraEdge’s procurement constraints? 2) Can procurement confirm PO timing if we land on Option B? If yes, I’ll circulate a redline-ready term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v2.docx) and loop in Marissa for final commercial approval.

I’ll also attach a drafted counter with numbers so procurement has something concrete to review (attachment: redwood_counter_options.pdf).

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--- Original attached: AuroraEdge_Renewal_Request.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal request + sprint credits / temporary price guard

Internal thread — quick alignment ask. I proposed A/B/C options to the customer and recommended B. Need Marissa (commercial) and Ben (finance) to confirm feasibility and final numbers so I can push the term sheet.

Summary of recommended commercial structure (Option B):
- Commit bump: +20% (moving to quarterly true-up cadence) — estimated incremental ARR impact: $145k annualized
- Sprint credit: 50k token-equivalents applied as a one-time credit against first invoice after renewal
- Rate guard: 3-month temporary price hold on the bumped band; after 3 months price reverts to negotiated band unless extended via usage milestone
- PO timing incentive: additional 3% discount on bumped band if PO received by 2026-12-08

Open questions for Finance (Ben):
1) Can we absorb a 50k sprint credit and a 3% early-PO incentive while maintaining target margin on this deal?
2) If we provide a 3-month rate guard, do we want a usage cap clause (e.g., if usage > 2x forecast, automatic reprice)?

Open questions for Commercial (Marissa):
1) Are there any legal/commercial clauses you want included for the temporary guard (auto-reprice, expiration trigger)?
2) If the customer asks to extend to 6 months, what approval path do we need?

Attached: redwood_counter_options.pdf (draft numbers) and a sketch of the term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v2.docx).

Please reply with quick 'approve' / 'need changes' so I can get back to Sasha before EOD.

— Vivek

(attachment: redwood_counter_options.pdf (pdf), redwood_term_sheet_v2.docx (docx))

From: Sasha Petrova <sasha@auroraedge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auroraedge.com
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + sprint credits / temporary price guard

Vivek — thanks for the options and the quick turnaround. AuroraEdge is comfortable with Option B pending two small tweaks: 1) a clear usage gate for the rate guard (if we exceed 2.5x forecast in month 1, the guard pauses), and 2) confirmation that the 50k sprint credit can be split (30k onboarding / 20k launch-day).

If you can send the DocuSign link and a redline with those two items, we’ll route the PO and target sign-off by 12/08. We appreciate the early-PO incentive — that helps.

Best,
Sasha
Head of Platform, AuroraEdge
(looking forward to the DocuSign link)
